title: Zscaler cloud architecture
aliases: how is a zscaler cloud built

prose.text: What Zscaler runs on a tenant's behalf, component by component, and where the two main services part ways. {{three-components}}

steps.label: Which cloud?
steps.text: A tenant lives on one named cloud: [[shared.cloud-architecture.cloud-names]].

steps.label: Control plane.
steps.text: The Central Authority holds policy and configuration, built differently per service: [[shared.cloud-architecture.central-authority]].

steps.label: Data plane.
steps.text: Service Edges inspect traffic and enforce policy, in public, private and virtual forms: [[shared.cloud-architecture.service-edges]]. A subcloud narrows which edges a tenant uses: [[shared.subclouds]].

steps.label: Logs.
steps.text: Log Routers, Nanolog clusters, NSS and LSS: [[shared.cloud-architecture.logging-path]].

steps.label: Supporting systems and feeds.
steps.text: Sandbox and PAC servers, the Admin Console, and Feed Central: [[shared.cloud-architecture.support-systems]].

steps.label: Private Access tunnels and trust.
steps.text: Z-Tunnels and Microtunnels in [[shared.cloud-architecture.tunnels]], certificates in [[shared.cloud-architecture.trust-model]].

steps.label: When something fails.
steps.text: Per component, including the Business Continuity Cloud and client fail-open: [[shared.cloud-architecture.failure-domains]].

prose.text: {{zpa-separate}} {{zpa-without-zia}} [[zpa.troubleshooting.no-access:other-traffic-elsewhere]] {{separate-stacks}} What, if anything, links the two stacks for one tenant is open {{gap:cross-product-linkage}}.

prose.label: Making changes live.
prose.text: A ZIA change is saved but not live until activated: [[zia.api.activation:saved-not-live]]. Which products stage changes behind an activation at all is in [[shared.activation]]; whether a ZPA write needs any such step is open: [[zpa.api.activation:write-takes-effect]].

prose.label: Names.
prose.text: Older names for these components (ZEN, broker, Z-App) are mapped in [[shared.terminology]].

three-components.statement: Zscaler describes its Internet & SaaS cloud infrastructure as three key components: the Central Authority, the Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS, and Nanolog clusters.

quotes: The highly scalable, global, multi-cloud infrastructure features three key components: the Zscaler Central Authority (CA), Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS (ZIA), and Nanolog clusters.

zpa-separate.statement: Private Access was built from the ground up for secure remote access and runs on its own multi-tenant infrastructure, separate from Internet & SaaS; the separation ensures that when one organization uses both services, public and internal traffic never mix on the same device.

quotes: Private Access (ZPA) was built from the ground up to provide secure remote access.
Private Access runs on a unique multi-tenant infrastructure, separate from that of Internet & SaaS, to make the service highly available.
This separation ensures that when the same organization is using both services, public and internal traffic never mix on the same device.

zpa-without-zia.statement: An organization does not need Internet & SaaS to use Private Access. When it uses both, Client Connector inherits some functionality from Internet & SaaS, such as enrollment, user profiles and traffic management.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector inherits some functionality from Internet & SaaS, including enrollment, user profiles, traffic management, etc.
However, organizations do not need access to Internet & SaaS to use Private Access.

separate-stacks.statement: A tenant using both services therefore deals with two sets of components: the Internet & SaaS Central Authority, Public Service Edges and Nanolog with NSS, and the Private Access Central Authority, Service Edges and Log Streaming Service.
separate-stacks.conditions: Composed from the two architecture articles and the LSS article; no source lists the per-service components side by side.

cross-product-linkage.title: What links a tenant's Internet & SaaS and Private Access infrastructure
cross-product-linkage.detail: Unverified legacy statement: a tenant using both services has separate CA, Service Edge and LSS/Nanolog instances per product, "linked via the shared Zscaler PKI and Zscaler Identity layer". The architecture articles describe each service's PKI on its own and do not describe a shared identity or PKI layer between them.
cross-product-linkage.blocks: reasoning about whether an identity or certificate change in one service affects the other
